name: KURMA

variants.depicted: Black giant tortoise Kurma supporting Mandara through the churning of the Ocean of Milk, viewed close at waterline.
variants.anatomy: ONE enormous BLACK tortoise, one tortoise head, two eyes, one broad domed shell, FOUR stout reptilian legs, one small natural tortoise tail. Complete animal form, NO humanoid torso, extra arms, fish tail, weapons, crown or ornaments. Reverent portrayal of Vishnu's tortoise avatar. [kurma-c01, kurma-c33, kurma-c36, kurma-c43, kurma-c28]
variants.moment: Brace his huge front legs against the moving water while lifting his mighty head toward the near viewer under the mountain's immense burden. Eyes composed and unwavering, never monster-like. His wet head dominates foreground and the mountain rises clearly from the shell behind it.
variants.power: Support the actual Mount Mandara resting directly on his shell while the Ocean of Milk is churned; turbulent pale water and heavy foam surge around his limbs, no glowing energy. A single serpent coil around the mountain is Vasuki used as a rope, secondary and not part of Kurma's anatomy. [kurma-c35, kurma-c36, kurma-c39, kurma-c41]
variants.setting: The primordial Ocean of Milk in the mountain-churning episode. [kurma-c03, kurma-c39]
variants.camera: Extreme close waterline low-angle portrait of head and front shell, full mountain contact point readable behind; mountain is a physical scale reference, never a tiny decorative rock. Kurma occupies most of frame.
variants.light: Single warm dawn slit above the churning waters, bronze rim light on black wet shell and powerful deep shadow.
